newsitem.title: JAPAN: Unidentified ship fires on Japanese fishing boat.
newsitem.headline: Unidentified ship fires on Japanese fishing boat.

text.p: An unidentified ship fired on a Japanese fishing boat near Russian-held islands disputed by Japan, injuring two fishermen, a Japanese coastguard spokesman said on Thursday.
The 4.7-tonne trawler Eiko-maru, with three crewmen, was fired on in waters near Habomai Island late on Wednesday, the spokesman for Japan's Maritime Safety Agency (MSA) said.

Crewmember Nobuyuki Maehara, 42, was seriously injured with a bullet through his thigh and another crewmen, Sakae Sawano, 35, was also slightly injured. Both were taken to hospital in the Japanese port of Nemuro, the MSA spokesman said.
The agency has not yet been able to confirm the nationality of the ship which fired on the trawler, the spokesman said.
A dense fog had cut visibility in the area at the time and it was not clear whether the Eiko-maru was in Japanese waters or on the Russian side of the demarcation line, he said.
Following the incident, Japan's Foreign Ministry asked the Russian government to check if Russian patrol vessels were involved in the shooting.
"If the Russians were involved in the shooting, such an act against unarmed fishing vessels cannot be condoned," top government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a news conference.
The Russians have not yet responded to Japan's inquiry, Kajiyama said.
Moscow has repeatedly accused Japanese fishing boats of poaching in Russian waters.
Last August, Russian patrol boats opened fire on two small Japanese fishing boats in the area, seriously injuring two crewmen.
Habomai and three other islands, called the Northern Territories by Japan and the Southern Kuriles by Russia, were seized by the Soviet Army in the last days of World War Two.

Japan has refused to sign a World War Two peace treaty with Moscow without the return of the islands, located northeast of Hokkaido, one of Japan's four main islands. The two countries normalised relations in 1956.
